title: AI Discovers Unstable Fluid Blow-Up Singularities to Near-Machine Precision
whyItMatters: Physics-informed neural networks discovered new families of unstable self-similar blow-up singularities in 3D Euler and porous-media fluid PDEs at GPU double-precision accuracy.
summary: Researchers from NYU, Google DeepMind, Stanford, and Brown paired physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with a high-precision Gauss–Newton optimizer to locate elusive unstable self-similar blow-up profiles in nonlinear fluid equations. Reaching near-double-float machine precision (~10⁻¹³ residual), the discovered profiles cross the precision threshold required for rigorous computer-assisted mathematical blow-up proofs and revealed a clean asymptotic scaling law.
technicalHighlights: Discovered multiple new families of unstable self-similar blow-up solutions for 3D Euler with boundary and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations.
Achieved near-double-float GPU round-off accuracy, overcoming the ~10⁻³ error ceiling that previously barred PINNs from rigorous PDE proofs.
Uncovered an empirical asymptotic law relating blow-up rate to instability order, informing subsequent Navier–Stokes blow-up research.
caveats: Supplies ultra-high-precision numerical profiles rather than complete formal proofs on its own; rigorous existence proofs require follow-up interval-arithmetic certification.

scoreRationale.foundational: Opened a systematic AI-driven window into unstable PDE blow-up singularities previously invisible to standard numerics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Provided a key computational playbook directly feeding 2026 computer-assisted attacks on Euler and Navier–Stokes blow-up.
scoreRationale.verification: Residuals verified to near-machine precision with reproducible PDE checks; journal review ongoing.
scoreRationale.velocity: Turned fragile, infinitely-tuned unstable PDE searches into repeatable high-precision neural optimization.
